text_At Rigshospitalet in Copenhagen, me: At Rigshospitalet in Copenhagen, medical students encountered life after a total laryngectomy through the words and demonstrations of someone who lives it every day.
text_I was invited to contribute my own: I was invited to contribute my own experience of cancer, my voice after surgery, and the everyday life that follows treatment. The students could see and hear how my voice works in practice and ask the questions that do not always appear in a textbook.

text_This is a story about finding my fe: This is a story about finding my feet again. About humour, hope and discovering that life can still be good, even when it turns out differently from what I had planned.
Some days stay with you forever.
text_Some moments divide life into befor: Some moments divide life into before and after.
text_For me, it was the day I received t: For me, it was the day I received the news that changed everything.
text_Suddenly, my days revolved around g: Suddenly, my days revolved around getting through the next day. Plans, work and dreams for the future had to wait.
text_But I kept my joy in life.”: But I kept my joy in life.”
text_After the operation, the silence wa: After the operation, the silence was almost the most overwhelming part.
text_I had to learn a completely new way: I had to learn a completely new way to communicate with other people, and even with myself.
It took time. And it took patience.
text_Humour has never taken away the ser: Humour has never taken away the seriousness of it all.
It has made it easier to carry.
